summary: Build a password-locked binary that computes your secretly-assigned function. Post it publicly. Figure out everyone else's function before their binary locks.

phases.name: Reverse-engineering warm-ups
phases.description: Four standalone RE challenges of increasing difficulty. Each binary hides a flag that unlocks when you defeat its password defense. Submitting a flag scores qualifier points and unlocks the arena.

levels.defense: password never stored; verified by hash/constraints

phases.name: CTF finale
phases.description: Short multi-stage capstone board feeding final standings.

submission.validation: On upload you privately declare your assigned function id and password. The server instantiates the module in a sandbox, writes the password, and asserts run(a,b) == f(a,b) on random inputs, and that a wrong password returns the WRONG_PASSWORD sentinel. Only honest, working binaries go public.

scoring.rationale: With 10 options and +2/-2, guessing without real signal loses points on average. Well-defended binaries net positive from wrong guesses.

lock.effect: Once a binary receives 5 guess attempts (correct or wrong, from 5 distinct guessers), it is locked. No further guesses are accepted against it.

protocol.idempotency: GET endpoints are side-effect-free; POST /guess and POST /upload are not idempotent and are subject to the lock and rate-limit rules.
